newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Komineft to slash workforce.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Komineft to slash workforce.

text.p: Russian oil company Komineft plans to make deep cuts in its workforce by the end of 1997, Vitaly Pinchuk, deputy chief executive in charge of finances, said on Thursday.
"If at the beginning of this year there were about 18,000 people working for us...by the end of this year, about nine or 10,000 people will be working for us," he said.
Komineft, the main production unit of oil holding company KomiTEK, produced around 5.2 million tonnes of oil last year, including via joint ventures.
Earlier on Thursday the company announced a 1996 pre-tax loss of 254.3 billion roubles according to Russian accounting standards.
It had already cut staff to between 15,000 and 16,000 when it disposed of its transport, supply, farming and other non-core activities.
Pinchuk said Komineft was keeping up with tax payments and expected to settle an outstanding 500 billion rouble tax bill to the government and other state bodies in 1998.
"Barring any force majeure, I think in 1998 we have a real chance of settling up, especially since when we finish restructuring...our liability for taxes will go down," he said.
He said that, depending on the success of its restructuring, Komineft could even turn a profit in 1998.
